A set of recordings

Source: R/RecordingSet.R
recordingSet.Rd

A RecordingSet is a data frame with one row for each recording, holding what is known of each recording without reading it. It is what an analysis of many recordings is run over, wherever they come from. Each place that recordings come from describes them in its own way, and is mapped onto the same columns here, so that sets from different places can be combined with rbind().

Usage

recordingSet(x, ...)

# Default S3 method
recordingSet(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'character'
recordingSet(x, source = NA_character_, ...)

# S3 method for class 'data.frame'
recordingSet(x, ...)

Arguments

x

Paths of audio files, or a data frame with at least the columns uri and location.

...

Not used.

source

For files, the collection they are from: one value for all of them, or one for each.

Value

A RecordingSet.

Details

Every set has these columns, in this order, with NA where a value is not known:

  • uri: what the recording is, unique within the set and never NA. A recording held by audioBlast has the address audioBlast gives it, https://api.audioblast.org/recording/{source}/{id}, and a file the file:// address of its path.

  • source: the collection the recording is from, e.g. "xeno-canto".

  • location: where the audio can be read from, a path or a URL.

  • hash: the SHA-256 hash of the file, in lower case.

  • duration: in seconds.

  • sample_rate: in Hz.

  • channels: the number of channels.

  • codec: the format the audio is in, e.g. "mp3" or "pcm_s16le".

  • status: how measuring the file went, "ok", "missing" or "unreadable", or NA where it has not been measured.

  • start: when the recording began, in UTC. It is given only where the time zone the recording was made in is known, and is never guessed.

  • tz: the time zone the recording was made in.

  • lat, lon: where the recording was made, in decimal degrees.

  • taxon: what the recording is of.

  • author, license, rights_holder: who made the recording, the URL of its licence, and who holds the rights in it. A licence that is NA is one that is not known, not one that leaves the recording free to use.

Any other columns a source gives follow these. An empty string in one of the columns above is taken to be a value that is not known, and is NA.

Several recordings can be of one file: the Animal Sound Archive lists a recording of several species once for each of them. Recordings that share a hash or a location are counted as one file.

Making a set from files checks that they exist but reads nothing from them, so their measurements are NA. audioblast() with output="RecordingSet" gives a set of recordings held by audioBlast, with what audioBlast has measured of their files.

Subsetting a set keeps it a set while the uri and location columns remain, and gives a plain data frame once either is dropped. Sets are combined with rbind(), with a set as the first argument: a column that only some of the sets have is NA in the rows of the others.

See also

audioblast() for a set of recordings held by audioBlast.

Examples

f <- system.file("extdata", "AUDIOMOTH.WAV", package="sonicscrewdriver")
recordingSet(f, source="AudioMoth")
#> <RecordingSet: 1 recording of 1 file, from 1 source>
#>                                                                            uri
#>  file:///home/runner/work/_temp/Library/sonicscrewdriver/extdata/AUDIOMOTH.WAV
#>     source duration sample_rate channels status
#>  AudioMoth       NA          NA       NA   <NA>
#> Other columns: location, hash, codec, start, tz, lat, lon, taxon,
#>   author, license, rights_holder

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
rs <- audioblast("data", "recordings", source="bio.acousti.ca",
                 max_pages=1, output="RecordingSet")
rbind(rs, recordingSet(f))
} # }
